title: Probabilistic geo-preference with capacity-scaling guardrails
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Implement a probabilistic, capacity-aware geo preference layer that balances user locality (geo-pinning) with global throughput constraints and graceful failure modes. This ticket covers: algorithm design, simulator, conservative rollout, and production observability. The behavior should preserve locality where possible (to meet p50/p95 latency SLOs for local requests) while automatically diverting excess load to other regions when capacity or latency budgets are exhausted. It must integrate with existing circuit-breaker signals and token-based shedding so that on heavy load the system degrades predictably rather than failing hard.
background: Current steering policies are deterministic: prefer local region then failover. This causes hot-spots when a single region sees bursty traffic that exceeds its GPU pools; either requests queue up (tail latency explosions) or brute failover floods peer regions causing cascading throttles. We want a softer, probabilistic preference that gives a controlled fraction of traffic a chance to use remote capacity early and reserve local headroom for latency-sensitive requests. Also needs to be capacity-aware: use real-time capacity scores from the allocator and respect circuit-breaker states for model variants and region-level SLO alarms.
acceptance_criteria: Algorithm implemented as steering module that returns per-request candidate region list and probability weights
Local-pinning probability configurable per-customer and per-route (default 0.85), with support for time-varying schedules
Capacity score integration: region_score in range [0.0,1.0] derived from available tokens, queue length, GPU utilization and autoscaler horizon
Circuit breaker signals respected: any region with open breaker receives zero routing weight

Token-based shedding: when global capacity budget exhausted, module emits explicit "shed" decision with reason code and suggested fallback (e.g., smaller model variant, cache-hit serve, or HTTP 503-with-retry-after)
Simulation results show 20-40% reduction in p99 tail latency in overloaded scenarios vs current deterministic failover (include sim harness in PR)
End-to-end integration tests exercising: local overload, cross-region overload, intermittent region flapping, and cold-start capacity ramp
Gradual rollout plan with metric gates (see rollout_plan) is included and validated in staging cluster
design_notes: Steering uses three inputs: locality_score (binary sticky pin), capacity_score (0..1), and latency_estimate (moving quantile from telemetry)
Final weight for region r = base_locality_weight * locality_boost(r) * capacity_score(r) * latency_factor(r). We then normalize across candidate regions and sample probabilistically.
Locality_boost is a tunable multiplier: when we want stronger geo-pinning raise to 1.5; to allow aggressive spill raise to 0.7
Latency_factor uses a soft penalty derived from p95/p99 deviation from SLO target. Regions exceeding latency fence (p99 > 2x SLO) are penalized heavily
We will maintain per-customer sticky buckets with TTL (default 10 minutes) so sampling remains probabilistically consistent for short sessions
Circuit breaker integration: three states (closed, half-open, open). Open => weight 0; half-open => allow fixed probe rate (1-2%)
Tokenized shedding approach: allocate a small holding quota per-region for low-latency tokens; when exhausted, prefer smaller model or cached response and emit shed telemetry
implementation_plan: 1) Build routing module and plugin hooks in request director (runtime) - Diego
2) Add capacity_score output in allocator service (PR: github.com/redwood/allocator/pull/487) - depends on ENG-614900
3) Implement probabilistic sampler and sticky-bucket store (in-memory with bounded size + Redis fallback)
4) Wire circuit-breaker status API into steering module
5) Add unit & integration tests; create simulator scenario files
6) Create feature flag gate and staged rollout config in config-service
7) Dashboard and alerting config in Grafana/Alertmanager
8) Rollout to staging, run chaos experiments, then gradual prod rollout
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged behind 'prob_geo_pref' with default off for existing routes
Canary cohort: 1% of traffic globally for 48h. Gate: no increase in global error rate; p99 latency per-customer must not increase >5%
Phase 2: 10% for 24h, run targeted overload scenarios (synthesize traffic) and validate shedding paths
Phase 3: 50% for 24h, confirm autoscaler behaviour remains stable
Full: flip default to enabled for new customers; existing customers opt-in via config; provide kill-switch to revert to deterministic policy
Gates include: region-level open circuit events should not exceed baseline by >1.5x, shed_rate must be within expected bounds, and no manual emergency invokes
telemetry_dashboards: Grafana: Routing -> ProbGeoPref -> per-region weight heatmap
Grafana: Steer -> Shed Rate and Reasons
SLO Dashboard: per-route p50/p95/p99 latency with cohort comparison (canary vs baseline)
Tracing: sample traces with cross-region routing to validate KV cache hit behavior
